             SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY’S VERIFIED
                 MOTION FOR ENTRY OF PROTECTIVE ORDER

       Southwestern Public Service Company’s (“SPS”) Application requests authority to change

its base rates and other associated relief. To facilitate the discovery process, SPS moves the New

Mexico Public Regulation Commission to (“Commission”) enter a Protective Order, substantially

in the form attached as Exhibit A, to govern the disclosure and use of confidential, competitively

sensitive, and proprietary information by SPS, the Commission’s Utility Division Staff (“Staff”),

and any other parties in relation to this case. In support of this Motion, SPS states the following:

       1.      Staff and Intervenors to this proceeding may seek documents and other information

during discovery or for use at hearing that is confidential, competitively sensitive, and proprietary,

and that should remain nonpublic. SPS may submit similar discovery requests to the other parties.

The requested Protective Order will permit the parties to respond to future discovery requests for

confidential or proprietary information without delay caused by seeking a protective order at the

time each request seeking confidential or proprietary information is issued.
        2.      The Commission is authorized under NMSA 1978, Sections 14-2-1(F) & (L), and

Section 62-6-17(C) to protect confidential or proprietary information and trade secrets from public

disclosure.

       3.      1.2.2.8(B) NMAC of the Commission’s Procedural Rules governs requests for

entry of appropriate protective orders to prevent public disclosure of confidential and proprietary

information.

       4.      The Commission typically enters appropriate protective orders to establish

conditions for the disclosure and use of confidential, competitively sensitive, and proprietary

information. The form of Protective Order attached to this motion as Exhibit A is identical in

substance to the protective order that was issued in SPS’s ongoing Certificate of Public

Convenience and Necessity proceeding, Case No. 25-00066-UT.

       5.      SPS requested, via email, positions on this Motion and received the following

responses: Staff – does not oppose; New Mexico Department of Justice – did not provide response;

New Mexico Large Customer Group – does not oppose; Occidental Permian Ltd. – does not

oppose; Louisiana Energy Services LLC – does not oppose; Federal Executive Agencies – does

not oppose; Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy – takes no position; Prosperity Works – takes

no position; Walmart, Inc. – does not oppose; Targa Resources Corp. – does not oppose; New

Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department – does not oppose.

       For the reasons stated, SPS respectfully moves the Commission to issue a protective order

substantially in the form of Exhibit A to this Motion.

                            [PROPOSED] PROTECTIVE ORDER
       THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon the Verified Motion for Protective Order filed by Southwestern Public

Service Company (“SPS”) (“Motion”). Being fully informed of the premises, the Commission

FINDS and CONCLUDES as follows:

       1.      SPS’s Motion states that during discovery parties may seek documents and other

information that may contain confidential or proprietary information that should not be publicly

disclosed. SPS states that issuance of a protective order will permit parties to respond to future

requests for confidential or proprietary information without the delay caused by seeking a

protective order at the time each request seeking confidential or proprietary information is issued.

       2.      Referencing NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1(F) and (L), and 62-6-17(C), SPS requests a

Protective Order to be able to provide certain Confidential Material (as defined below) to parties

herein pursuant to Confidentiality Agreements with those parties. SPS submitted a form of

proposed Protective Order, including the Confidentiality Agreement, which it asserted is

substantively the same form of the Protective Order issued by the Commission in recent
 proceedings. SPS states that the Commission is authorized by law to provide protection from

public disclosure of confidential or proprietary information and trade secrets and that, pursuant to

1.2.2.8(A) and (B) NMAC, the Commission is authorized to enter appropriate protective orders to

prevent public disclosure of confidential information.

       3.      SPS’s Motion for Protective Order indicates that SPS sought the positions of the

parties, and no party who responded opposed the motion.

       4.      Under Rule 1.2.2.8(A) NMAC, it is the policy of the Commission to allow full and

complete access to public records in accordance with the Inspection of Public Records Act

(“IPRA”). NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1 to -12. Section 14-2-5 of the IPRA provides that, “[r]ecognizing

that a representative government is dependent upon an informed electorate, the intent of the

legislature in enacting the [IPRA] is to ensure, and it is declared to be the public policy of this

state, that all persons are entitled to the greatest possible information regarding the affairs of

government and the official acts of public officers and employees.” NMSA 1978, § 14-2-5. Section

14-2-1(H) provides that “[e]very person has a right to inspect public records of this state except …

as otherwise provided by law.” The IPRA defines the term “public records” (disclosure of which

is required unless an exception applies) broadly to include not only records created by or required

to be kept by an agency, but also any other documents “received, maintained or held by or on

behalf of any public body [that] relate to public business.” NMSA 1978, § 14-2-6(G). Parties

therefore should avoid designating documents as confidential that would not be entitled to such

protection under IPRA.

       5.      The Commission finds that SPS has made a sufficient showing to justify the

issuance of a protective order. It therefore is appropriate to issue a Protective Order in substantially

the same form as the protective order attached to SPS’s Motion as Exhibit A.



                                                   2
        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      The Motion for Entry of Protective Order is GRANTED to the extent provided by,

and subject to, the terms and conditions of this Protective Order.

       B.      This Protective Order establishes a procedure to facilitate discovery among the

Parties and to provide for the expeditious handling of information that a party claims is

Confidential Material, as that term is defined below. This Protective Order shall not be construed

as a ruling on the confidentiality of any document.

       C.      Designating Information as Confidential

               1.      This Protective Order provides protection for confidential and proprietary

information identified and clearly marked by parties as “CONFIDENTIAL MATERIAL”

(hereinafter referred to as “Confidential Material”). Material may only be designated as

confidential if the disclosing party can establish the material is not in the public domain and is

protected by applicable law, including IPRA, the New Mexico Trade Secrets Act or as otherwise

provided by law. No material shall be treated as Confidential Material if it: (a) is in the public

domain at the time of disclosure; (b) becomes part of the public domain through no fault of a party

who received it under this Protective Order; (c) is in the lawful possession of the receiving party

at the time it is disclosed under this Protective Order; (d) is or has been received by a party on a

non-restricted basis from a third party that has the right to make such a disclosure; or (e) has been

or becomes disclosed as non-confidential material in any other legal or regulatory proceeding.

               2.      All material submitted to the Commission as provided below or furnished

to other parties pursuant to any request for information, subpoena, or other mode of discovery that

is claimed to be of a trade secret, proprietary, or confidential nature and protectable under IPRA

shall be clearly marked “CONFIDENTIAL MATERIAL” by the party claiming protection. If a



                                                 3
 document contains both confidential and non-confidential information, the party claiming

confidentiality shall claim protection only for the portions of the document which satisfy the

standards for confidential treatment and clearly identify the specific portions of the document for

which confidentiality is claimed. For Confidential Material filed with the Commission or furnished

to a party, each page containing Confidential Material shall be printed on pink-colored paper, if a

hard copy is filed or transmitted. The page color should be changed to pink for documents filed or

transmitted electronically, such as for an in-camera inspection by the Hearing Examiner under

Paragraphs I.2 or K.1.d below.

       D.      Segregation of Files

       Access to and review of Confidential Material shall be strictly controlled by the terms of

this Order. Confidential Material provided in response to discovery requests shall not be filed with

the Commission. The original and all copies of Confidential Material filed with the Commission

shall be filed in a sealed envelope or box, which envelope or box shall be marked by the submitting

party “CONFIDENTIAL - SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER IN CASE NO. 25-00079-UT,”

and shall be segregated in the files of the Commission and withheld from inspection by any person

except under the conditions established in this Order unless such Confidential Material is released

from the restrictions of this Order either through agreement of the parties or, after notice to the

parties and hearing, pursuant to the Order of the Commission and/or binding order of a court

having jurisdiction.

       E.      Confidentiality Agreement

       No access to Confidential Material shall be authorized under the terms of this Order until

the person desiring access to such material signs a Confidentiality Agreement in the form attached

hereto and incorporated herein. Such executed Confidentiality Agreement shall be filed with the



                                                 4
 Commission and a copy served on the parties as required by Rule 1.2.2.10 NMAC and applicable

orders in this case prior to inspection of the documents. Commissioners, their advisory staff and

expert consultants, attorneys in the Commission’s Office of General Counsel, and the Hearing

Examiner are not required to sign the Confidentiality Agreement to view Confidential Material.

       F.      Availability to the Commission and Parties

       Except as otherwise provided in this Order, the only persons to be permitted access to the

Confidential Material, other than the Commissioners, their advisory staff, attorneys in the

Commission’s Office of General Counsel, and the Hearing Examiner, are Commission Staff,

parties to this case and their employees and legal counsel, including staff and expert witnesses

working with counsel, who have executed the Confidentiality Agreement in the form appended to

this Order as Attachment A.

       G.      Availability to Non-Signatories

       All persons who are on the official service list and who have not executed the

Confidentiality Agreement shall receive, on the date that it is filed, the Affidavit required under

Paragraph K(l)(c), K(2)(b), and K(3)(b) and all non-confidential portions of any documents

marked as Confidential Material in redacted form.

       H.      Preservation of Confidentiality

       Persons afforded access to any Confidential Material by reason of this Order shall not use

or disclose the Confidential Material for purposes of business or competition, or any other purpose

other than the purpose of preparation of and conduct of this proceeding (except as provided in

paragraph N), including preparation of and conduct of any appeals arising from this proceeding.

Persons afforded access to Confidential Material shall use such information solely as contemplated

herein and shall take all reasonable precautions to keep the Confidential Material secure as trade



                                                 5
 secret, confidential, or proprietary information and in accordance with the purposes and intent of

this Order. Such persons shall not discuss the contents thereof with anyone other than persons who

have executed the Confidentiality Agreement, and shall not, in any manner, reveal, disclose,

publish or make known the contents of the Confidential Material to anyone else except as

otherwise provided in this Order. No person may copy, microfilm, microfiche or otherwise

reproduce the information without the written consent of the party claiming protection except for

his or her own use, or the use of persons permitted access to the information and who have signed

a Confidentiality Agreement.

       I.      Challenges to Claims of Confidentiality

       Staff or a party may at any time challenge a claim by a party owning or holding Confidential

Material that the Confidential Material is confidential. In the event of such a challenge, the

following procedures shall apply:

       1.      Staff or the party asserting the challenge shall: (i) first contact counsel for the

providing party and attempt to resolve any differences informally and, if the parties cannot resolve

the disagreement informally, (ii) file a motion with the Commission for a ruling on the challenge

(referred to hereinafter as a “Request for Confidentiality Determination”). Copies of a Request for

Confidentiality Determination shall be served on Staff and all parties to this proceeding.

       2.      When a Request for Confidentiality Determination has been filed and served, the

owner or holder of the Confidential Material shall, within three business days of service thereof,

deliver (as distinguished from file) in person, by regular mail, or email all of the relevant

Confidential Material to the Commission or the Presiding Officer if such as been designated for

an in camera inspection.




                                                 6
         3.      The owner or holder of the Confidential Material shall, without order or action by

the Commission and within five business days after a Request for Confidentiality Determination

has been served on it, file its initial brief and supporting affidavit stating in detail the basis for its

confidentiality claims and shall request a hearing on the matter. The brief and supporting affidavit

shall be e-mailed, faxed, or hand-delivered to the person seeking the confidentiality determination

on the day of filing. Failure to file an initial brief and supporting affidavit shall be deemed a waiver

of the confidentiality claims. Within five business days after service of the initial brief and

supporting affidavit, the party or Staff that filed the Request for Confidentiality Determination

shall file a brief and supporting affidavit in response. Service shall be in like manner as the initial

brief and supporting affidavit. Within three business days of service of such response brief and

supporting affidavit, the owner or holder of the Confidential Material may file a reply brief, service

of which shall be in like manner as the previous briefs. Any other party or Staff may brief its

position, either opposing the owner or holder of Confidential Material in a brief filed five business

days after service of the initial brief or supporting non-disclosure in a brief filed within three

business days after service of the response brief of the party that filed the Request for

Confidentiality Determination. Service of any such briefs shall be in the manner required above.

        4.      The burden of proof to show the confidentiality of the Confidential Material shall

be on the party claiming confidentiality.

        5.      Staff and the parties shall not make public any information regarding disputed

alleged Confidential Material until the Commission rules on the claim of confidentiality. Following

a Commission ruling on confidentiality, the information shall be made available only pursuant to

the Commission’s order.

        J.      Requests Not to Disclose to Persons Signing Confidentiality Agreement



                                                    7
         If any party possessing Confidential Material wishes to decline to provide a specific party

with any or all Confidential Material which the possessor reasonably believes should be kept

confidential from such party notwithstanding the fact that such party may have executed the

Confidentiality Agreement, the party possessing the Confidential Material shall file a pleading

with the Commission prior to the time the Confidential Material is due to be produced, setting

forth the specific reasons that the Confidential Material should not be provided to such party. The

party denied access to the Confidential Material may then file a response within five business days

of service of the possessor’s pleading. The party seeking to preclude a certain party from receiving

Confidential Material shall have the burden of proof. The Confidential Material shall not be

produced to the challenged party pending a ruling by the Presiding Officer.

        K.      Use of Confidential Materials

                1.      Use by Staff and Parties

        If Staff or any party other than the party asserting the claim of confidentiality intends to

use any claimed Confidential Material in this proceeding in pre-filed testimony (including

exhibits) or at the hearing and even if Staff or the party using the Confidential Material does not

intend to challenge the claim of confidentiality, the following procedure shall apply:

                a.      Staff or the party intending to use the Confidential Material shall inform the

party asserting the claim of confidentiality of the intent and manner of use as follows: (i) for use

in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits), notice to be filed on the date the testimony is filed, and

(ii) for use at the hearing, notice to be provided to the Hearing Examiner and parties and Staff as

early as is feasible and preferably to be filed before the start of the hearing unless otherwise ordered

or approved. Within three business days of receiving notice of the intent to use Confidential

Material in pre-filed testimony or within two business days of receiving notice of the intent to use



                                                   8
 Confidential Material at the hearing or as otherwise ordered, the party claiming the confidentiality

of the Confidential Material shall inform Staff or the party intending to use the Confidential

Material whether it objects to public disclosure of the Confidential Material. If the party asserting

confidentiality fails to so notify the potential user, its objections shall be waived. Pending a ruling

on confidentiality, Staff or any party using Confidential Material in pre-filed testimony (including

exhibits) shall on the date that the notice is filed: (i) file a public version with the Confidential

Material redacted; (ii) file a confidential version under seal in accordance with the procedure in

Paragraph D above; and (iii) serve the confidential version on parties who have signed the

Confidentiality Agreement and the Presiding Officer.

               b.        If the party asserting the confidentiality of the Confidential Material objects

to public disclosure of the Confidential Material, it shall file a request seeking confidential

treatment of the material within three business days after it receives notice of the intended use of

Confidential Material in pre-filed testimony or within two business days after it receives notice of

the intended use of the Confidential Material at the hearing or as otherwise ordered.

               c.        Any request filed under Paragraph K(l)(b) shall include:

                         i.     An affidavit or affirmation consistent with the provisions of Rule

1.2.2.8(B)(1) NMAC that satisfies the claimant's burden of making a prima facie showing that

protection is appropriate for the particular information claimed to be Confidential Material and

must include, at a minimum, the following information with respect to each document marked

Confidential Material:

                                                (1) the date the Confidential Material was prepared;
                                                (2) the author of the Confidential Material;
                                                (3) a list of all persons, other than the disclosing party
                                                and its representatives, in possession of the
                                                Confidential
                                                Material;

                                                   9
                                                (4) the subject matter of the Confidential Material;
                                               (5) a description of the contents of the Confidential
                                               Material;
                                               (6) the number of pages which the Confidential
                                               Material
                                               comprises;
                                               (7) how the Confidential Material was acquired; and
                                               (8) the basis for all claims of confidentiality,
                                               including a
                                               showing that each document marked Confidential
                                               Material
                                               comes within one or more of the exceptions to the
                                               general
                                               disclosure requirement of the IPRA. NMSA 1978,
                                               § 14-2-I(A);

                                                      AND

                       ii.     A brief which sets forth the legal basis for protection and states

whether the public interest requires that the Confidential Material be used and whether an abstract

of or the extraction of specific information from the Confidential Material can be used as an

alternative.

        d.     The party asserting the confidentiality of the Confidential Material shall submit (as

distinguished from file) the relevant Confidential Material, under seal, by email to the Presiding

Officer for possible in camera inspection.

        e.     Within seven days of the filing of a request under Paragraph K(l)(b) or as otherwise

ordered, Staff or the party seeking to use the Confidential Material shall file a response addressing

the legal and factual merits of each confidentiality claim, including Staff’s or the party’s position

on whether the Confidential Material is in fact confidential. Any factual assertions in the response

shall be supported by a verifying affidavit.

               2.      Use by party asserting confidentiality




                                                 10
        If any party asserting the confidentiality of Confidential Material intends to use

Confidential Material in this proceeding, in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) or at the

hearing, the following procedures shall apply:

               a.      Such party shall file a notice of such intent, describing the manner of use

and requesting confidential treatment of its use of the material as follows: (i) for use in pre-filed

testimony (including exhibits), notice to be filed on the date the testimony is filed, and (ii) for use

at the hearing, notice to be provided to the Hearing Examiner and parties and Staff as early as is

feasible and preferably to be filed before the start of the hearing, unless otherwise ordered or

approved. Pending a ruling on confidentiality, the party using Confidential Material in pre-filed

testimony (including exhibits) shall, on the date that the notice is filed: (i) file a public version

with the Confidential Material redacted; (ii) file a confidential version under seal in accordance

with the procedure in Paragraph D; and (iii) serve the confidential version on parties who have

signed the Confidentiality Agreement and the Presiding Officer.

               b.      Such party shall file a request seeking confidential treatment of the material

on the date that the notice required under Paragraph K(2)(a) is filed. Such request shall include the

affidavit or affirmation and brief described in Paragraph K(l)(c).

               c.      Within seven days of the filing of a request under Paragraph K(2)(b), or as

otherwise ordered, Staff shall, and any Intervenor may, file a response addressing the legal and

factual merits of each confidentiality claim, including Staffs or the party's position on whether the

Confidential Material is in fact confidential. Any factual assertions in the response shall be

supported by a verifying affidavit or affirmation.

               3.      Bench Requests




                                                  11
                If the Hearing Examiner or Commission requires a party to file a document and the

party objects to public disclosure of the document or portions of the document, the following

procedure shall apply:

               a.        On or before the deadline for filing the document, the party shall (i) file a

public version of the document with the Confidential Material redacted; (ii) file a confidential

version of the document under seal in accordance with the procedure in Paragraph D; and (iii)

serve the confidential version on parties who have signed the Confidentiality Agreement and

Presiding Officer.

               b.        On or before the deadline for filing the document, the party shall file a

request seeking confidential treatment of the Confidential Material, including the affidavit and

brief described in Paragraph K(1)(c).

               c.        Within seven days of the filing of the request seeking confidential treatment

of the Confidential Material, or as otherwise order, Staff shall, and any Intervenor may, file a

response addressing the legal and factual merits of each confidentiality claim, including Staff’s or

the party’s position on whether the Confidential Material is in fact confidential. Any factual

assertions in the response shall be supported by a verifying affidavit or affirmation.

               4.        Rulings

                         a.     The Commission shall evaluate the materiality and relevance of the

Confidential Material to this case and, if necessary, determine whether the claimed Confidential

Material in fact contains confidential or proprietary information and, if so, determine whether the

public interest requires that the confidential or proprietary information be filed publicly or

produced at the hearing in this case, whether an abstract of or the extraction of specific information




                                                  12
 from the confidential or proprietary information be produced for use at the hearing, or whether the

Confidential Material shall be admitted and treated as a confidential exhibit.

                       b.     The Commission may issue a ruling on the requests under this

Paragraph based upon the affidavits and/or a hearing or other procedure determined by the

Commission. The Confidential Material shall remain confidential pending a ruling thereon by the

Commission. Following a Commission ruling on confidentiality, the information shall be available

strictly in conformity with the Commission’s order.

               5.      Hearings involving Confidential Material

               In the course of this proceeding, those portions of any hearings during which

Confidential Material obtained pursuant to the terms of this Order are likely to be disclosed shall

be conducted in a manner the Commission determines is consistent with the Open Meetings Act,

IPRA, the Public Utility Act and other relevant statutes.

               6.      Admissibility

               Staff and the parties retain the right to object to the admission into evidence of any

Confidential Material on any proper grounds, including relevance or materiality.


       L.      Appeal

       Sealed portions of the record in the proceeding may be forwarded to any court of competent

jurisdiction for purposes of an appeal, but under seal as designated herein for the information and

use of the court. If a portion of the record is forwarded to a court under seal for purposes of an

appeal, the providing party shall be notified which portion of the sealed record has been designated

by the appealing party as necessary to the record on appeal.

       M.      Continuation of Protection




                                                13
        Disclosure of Confidential Information is limited by this Order for two years from the date

of the final order, or final decision on appeal, whichever is later, provided that the Commission

may extend the period of protection upon a motion of a party filed prior to expiration of the period

of protection.

       N.        Use in Other Commission Proceedings

       Nothing in this order prohibits a person who executes the Confidentiality Agreement from

seeking to use Confidential Material in other Commission proceedings, subject to any applicable

rulings in such proceedings, and provided the original owner or holder of the Confidential Material

is served with the notice of intent to use Confidential Material. The procedure set forth in

Paragraph K(l) shall apply.

       O.        Filing and Delivery Pursuant to Commission Electronic Filing Policy

       Whenever the terms of this Order require the filing of pleadings or materials, such filings

are subject to the Commission’s Electronic Filing Policy then in effect. To the extent that this Order

requires confidential materials to be printed on pink colored paper for filing, if the filing is made

pursuant to the Commission’s Electronic Filing Policy, then such materials shall be prepared and

filed in accordance with Paragraph D above and mailed to the Records Bureau at Records Bureau,

New Mexico Public Regulation Commission, P.O. Box 1269, Santa Fe, New Mexico 87504.

Service of the filed documents shall be made to parties having filed Confidentiality Agreements

by emailed scanned versions of the materials in pink colored electronic format. To the extent that

this Order requires delivery of any materials to the Commission in connection with a Request for

Confidentiality Determination pursuant to Paragraph I.1, such delivery may be effected by email

to the Hearing Examiner assigned to this proceeding, without providing a copy of such materials

to any party or individual who has not executed a Confidentiality Agreement. The cover email



                                                 14
 delivering the document shall briefly describe the materials but shall not include any commentary

or argument. Notice of such delivery of the materials to the Hearing Examiner shall be emailed to

all parties and individuals on the approved service list.

        P.     For purposes of this Order, “Commission” means presiding officer, hearing

examiner, or the Commission, as appropriate in the context.

        Q.     The provisions of Rule 1.2.2.8(B) NMAC governing the procedures to be used

when any person desires to protect documents or information from disclosure are hereby waived

pursuant to Rule 1.2.2.8(D) NMAC.

        R.     Any person executing a Confidentiality Agreement consents to the jurisdiction of

the Commission and New Mexico courts for resolution of disputes regarding alleged violations of

this Order.

        S.     This Order is effective immediately.

        T.     A copy of this Order shall be served on all persons on the official service list for

this case.
